retained: Keep one thread per output, the single-kernel ABI, self-interaction skip, float32 softening, update ordering, and exact mass copy.
Use direct rsqrtf(distSq), apply one Newton refinement, and form the reciprocal cube with multiplies.
Retain target-mass scaling in the interaction coefficient and divide the accumulated force by targetMass after summation, rather than keeping the cancellation from the failed candidates.

retained: Replaced one-thread-per-output work with one warp per output; each lane sums source indices lane + 32k and the warp reduces all three force components.

Handled self-interaction and invalid output warps without early returns, so every lane participates in full-warp shuffles and only valid lane-zero threads store.

Assigning a complete warp to each output exposes parallelism across source indices while retaining the original pair-force arithmetic. This may improve utilization, but the changed summation order and performance require controller validation.
